summary: Model card for OpenAI Privacy Filter, a small (1.5B total / 50M active) open-weight bidirectional token classifier for PII detection and redaction derived from a gpt-oss-style checkpoint. Reports benchmark results on PII-Masking-300k and CredData, fine-tuning efficiency on SPY, and stress tests (clue position, multilingual, one-hop reasoning, adversarial formats), plus extensive limitations.

privacy.finding: The model itself is a privacy tool; strong PII detection but weaker on one-hop alias reasoning and some adversarial formats; authors stress it is not an anonymization guarantee.
privacy.quote: Privacy Filter is a redaction and data minimization aid, not an anonymization, compliance, or a safety guarantee.

multilingual_safety.finding: Detection quality degrades for lower-resource languages and scripts.
multilingual_safety.quote: Performance may drop on non-English text, non-Latin scripts, or naming patterns or domains that are out of distribution compared to model training.

bias_fairness.finding: Qualitative note that under-represented names and regional conventions may be missed; no bias eval.
bias_fairness.quote: names and identifiers that are underrepresented in training data, or that follow conventions different from the dominant training distribution, may be more likely to be missed or inconsistently bounded.

system_safeguards.finding: Positioned as one layer in privacy-by-design; recommends in-domain evaluation and human review for high-sensitivity workflows.
system_safeguards.quote: High-sensitivity workflows should also retain human review paths.

evals: adversarial confusion-category and confusing-format evals (classifier robustness)
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Adversarial evals test robustness of PII detection to confusing categories and formats (e.g., phonetic alphabet, line breaks); not jailbreaks of a chat model.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: In order to understand how Privacy Filter performs in adversarial settings that we might encounter in real data, we created various adversarial evaluations.

notable_new_eval_methods: Dataset label correction using GPT-5.4 adjudication with human verification (p.13)
One-hop alias-reasoning PII evals and clue-position stress tests (p.15-17)

self_reported_limitations.text: Not an anonymization, compliance or safety guarantee; static label policy requires fine-tuning to change.
One-hop reasoning remains difficult; recall degrades with distance of contextual cue.
Benchmark labels contained errors; model-based adjudication of dataset false positives reached only 85% agreement with humans and was not applied.
Span-level CredData scores lower due to boundary discrepancies.

notes: Not a generative model; no frontier-risk or conventional harmful-content evals. Classifier performance recorded under capability 'other'.
